mechaber/1:main: Whether it is permitted to roast two sheaves together and the laws of karmel. Containing 3 seifim: It is permitted to roast two sheaves together, and we are not concerned that perhaps moisture will pass from one to the other, for they are fruit juice and they do not cause chametzing.
mechaber/2:main: Vitika, which is a dish made from oil and salt with flour, is permitted, provided that it does not contain water. {Rama: And according to our custom, which is to be stringent with fruit juice, this too is forbidden.}
mechaber/3:main: Karmel that they flash in fire and grind—one may not cook its flour in water, lest it was not roasted well in fire and will become chametzed when cooked. And likewise when they crush new pots (meaning they put flour into the food to thicken), one may not cook in them, but only baked matzah that they returned and ground.
baer-heitev/2:_: And salt—even though salt causes chametzing as stated in siman 462, it is different here because it is nullified since it is minimal; and it is also possible that if there is much salt (or a little water—and some say this refers to honey in siman 462, where it discusses before Passover) we are concerned. Ran:
baer-heitev/3:א: Well. Specifically in karmel the Rambam is concerned about this; but regarding roasted flour the Rambam ruled in ch. 5 that it is permitted to cook l'chatchila. However the Mechaber concluded here only baked matzah, etc., implying he holds roasted flour is forbidden in every case; see Magen Avraham who wrote: it requires study whether if placed b'dieved in food they forbid because of this concern, for Rashi permits l'chatchila; and there is a difference regarding matzah kneaded with such flour and baked, as in siman 459, then placed in sauce—nevertheless it appears one should be stringent with matzah since matzah separates between flour and fire—end of his words. Chafetz Chayim wrote that in roasted karmel one should forbid even b'dieved; but in roasted flour, since per the Rambam it is permitted even l'chatchila, one may rely b'dieved to permit benefit or leave until after Passover—so it appears. See Bnei Chiya in siman 453:
baer-heitev/3:ב: The new ones. Beit Yosef explained they do so the first time to harden the pot—see Yad Ephraim:
baer-heitev/3:ג: And ground it. In Constantinople they forbid frying fish in baked matzah lest one confuse; but in doughnuts it is permitted—as Knesset HaGedolah expanded at length:
beer-hagolah/2:ב: Braita there, as explained in the siman above seif 2.
beer-hagolah/3:ג: Explanation that it is forbidden to use on Passover old pots:
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (s.k. 1) And salt, etc.—even though salt, etc.—this is Tur's question brought siman 462:
machatzit-hashekel/2:_: (s.k. 2) To be stringent, etc.—and siman 455 s.k. 16: since not stringent because it chametzs as minimal, rather fruit juice custom to be stringent—remedy to bake immediately if little salt fell on matzah:
machatzit-hashekel/3:א: (s.k. 3) This too, etc.—for roasting sheaves, etc.—even though in sheaves they only permitted from fruit juice:
machatzit-hashekel/3:ב: Not to make the mixture. Meaning not to mix fruit juice with flour because we are not concerned, etc., that Rava who permits and vitika holds fruit juice chametzs; nevertheless permitted since not only hardened. If it were full chametz with karet one should be concerned though uncommon; but since only hardened rabbinically, therefore no concern for uncommon moisture—especially for us who hold hardened is d'rabbanan as siman 442:
magen-avraham/2:א: And salt with flour. Even though salt chametzs as siman 462—say because minimal and form changed without power with oil; but real water we concern in any amount; possibly much salt we concern (Ran):
magen-avraham/2:ב: To be stringent with fruit juice. Implies not to forbid from salt as it is minimal as written—and siman 455:
magen-avraham/2:ג: This too forbidden. Taz implies roasting sheaves permitted—we are stringent not to mix by hand; but if comes naturally permitted—so Tosafos Menachot 54 permit from uncommon concern moisture:
magen-avraham/3:א: Meaning they put, etc.—this explanation is Tur's view; but Rabbeinu Yonah citing Rambam: new pots means they do so first time to harden pot—so Maharil and Bach. Requires study if placed b'dieved in food whether they forbid from this concern, for Rashi permits l'chatchila and Beit Yosef cites Rambam; difference regarding matzah kneaded with flour and baked as siman 459 then put in sauce—see there; nevertheless with matzah one should be stringent since matzah separates flour from fire:
magen-avraham/3:ב: And they ground it. In Constantinople they forbid making patties or frying fish in baked matzah lest confusion; in doughnuts permitted—see Knesset HaGedolah who expanded:
mishnah-berurah/1:_: (a) that they are fruit water - and the Omnipresent forbids placing a pitcher of moist grain in the hot oven that is made of toast, even though due to the heat of the oven, water may come out of the grain into the pitcher and be swallowed later by the toast of the body.
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (2) From oil and salt—even though our salt chametzs as end of siman 462—say because minimal and form changed from water form, no power with oil; but real water we concern in any amount; possibly also much salt water we concern:
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (2) (c) Permissible - Dashman hoi fruit water and there is no missing:
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (4) That it should not have water—but if it has water even any amount it is like fruit juice with water and chametzs; how much more if no oil in dish only water and salt with flour—certainly chametzs:
mishnah-berurah/2:ד: (4) (e) This is also prohibited - unless it is for a sick or old person and as above in the sign of the 17th 19th of the Haga. And the latter wrote that it is a DSA also to the Harma Shari Damalta that it is not common for the water to come out from one to the other and even if it came out not from the main point of the law. Deuteronomy:
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (1) (f) Carmel who is in love, etc. - RL even if his grain has already been eaten in the light, but his flour is as if baked, and K. L. Dafoy does not miss apah asor lest, etc.:
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (7) And will become chametzed, etc.—if they transgressed and placed in food the food is forbidden for benefit and forbidden to leave, for d'oraisa doubt:
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (8) When cooking it—even if flour itself was roasted in oven, do not cook in water lest not roasted well and come to chametz; some permit cooking roasted flour because fire heat dominates more than grain heat; several later authorities agreed one may rely b'dieved if made dish to permit benefit or leave until after Passover. Baked matzah with flour found inside—forbidden to put in sauce, for that flour certainly not baked well because matzah separates flour from fire; if placed it forbids dish even for benefit:
mishnah-berurah/3:ד: (9) Meaning they put flour, etc.—this explanation is Tur's view; but Beit Yosef citing Rambam new pots means they cook first time in new pots flour and water to harden and strengthen pot:
turei-zahav/1:_: From oil and salt. Ran wrote we do not forbid it as water mixed with oil since minimal and form changed without power with oil; but real water we concern in any amount; possibly much salt water we concern—end. We concern real water and do not say nullified in oil as with wine siman 462 (3) where nullified before Passover; here done on Passover:
turei-zahav/2:_: (17) Forbidden. Implies seif 1 permitted also for us. Reason we are stringent with fruit juice is not to mix by hand; but if comes naturally we leave to permitted law—and see siman 465:
turei-zahav/3:_: But only baked matzah. Tur wrote and in Gemara Rava said even baked matzah forbidden where workers common, etc.; Beit Yosef wrote no question, for Gemara has two versions and Rif and Rosh ruled like latter version; certainly Tur did not mean to challenge one version against one who rules other; rather his intent: since first version Rava said improper to permit where workers common i.e. Exilarch's house lest confusion with flour, and second version Rava himself did so where workers uncommon—if so why say Rava does not distinguish whether workers common—no legal difference, only whose action; wherever not evident to make dispute, certainly better to say so. And explain regarding lentils and legumes—for truly flour and more similar to five grains than baked matzah; Tur says even baked matzah stricter where workers common; though dispute on this, regarding lentil flour certainly concern, and we rule all legume and lentil flours forbidden—even whole forbidden lest confused with grain as 453—how much more here—as I see it:
